The current slugify implementation does the following:

- Converts input to lowercase
- Removes any characters that are not lowercase English letters, digits, whitespace, or hyphen (line 11 regex)
- Splits words by whitespace or hyphen (line 12)
- Joins words with separator (default '-')
- Enforces maxLength (default 50)

The problems per your requirements:

- It removes accented characters completely due to [^a-z0-9\s-] regex
- Underscores are removed and not treated as word separators
- Non-Latin symbols like emoji are removed (which is correct)
- No transliteration of accents

Plan to update slugify:

- Add transliteration for accented Latin letters to ASCII equivalents before regex removal
- Modify regex to keep underscores so they are treated as word separators
- Replace underscores with the separator (like spaces and hyphens)
- Keep dropping emoji and symbols as is

I will now research transliteration libraries or common approaches in JavaScript/TypeScript for accented Latin character transliteration.
